checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a P2P peer withhold cells to trigger incorrect polynomial recovery?

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P gossip validation layer for cell transmission. 2. Determine how cells are collected from multiple peers before recovery. 3. Simulate a scenario where a malicious peer withholds cells such that < 50% are available. 4. Verify the recovery function rejects this input before attempting polynomial interpolation. 5. If rejection fails, verify the resulting polynomial is incorrect. 6. Check if incorrect proofs generated from this polynomial would be accepted downstream. 7. Verify attestation validity checks would catch corrupted data.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Nodes: actor-p2p-peer, actor-validator-node. Attacker withholds cells to produce incorrect recovery output.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: What is the blast radius if recovery proceeds with insufficient cells?

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Trace the output of recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs to downstream consumers. 2. Identify which components rely on the recovered polynomial. 3. Determine if incorrect cells/proofs would propagate through the network. 4. Check if validator attestations would be affected by incorrect recovery. 5. Verify if there are secondary validation layers that would detect corruption. 6. Assess consensus impact: could incorrect proofs cause chain splits or finality issues? 7. Document the full attack chain from cell withholding to network impact.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bypassing threshold produces incorrect polynomial that generates incorrect cells and proofs propagating through the network.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is the cell count pre-condition checked before all other operations?

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function entry point. 2. Verify cell count check is the first validation after basic parameter parsing. 3. Ensure no allocations or cryptographic setup occurs before the threshold check. 4. Verify rejection returns immediately without partial processing. 5. Check that the function signature enforces input types that prevent bypassing the check. 6. Verify the pre-condition is documented in function specification.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Pre-condition must be checked before any resource-intensive operations.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are cell_indices validated for uniqueness and ascending order before polynomial recovery?

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function and its entry point validation. 2. Identify where cell_indices is parsed and validated. 3. Verify uniqueness check: attempt to submit duplicate cell_indices (e.g., [0, 0, 1, 2]) and verify rejection. 4. Verify ascending order check: attempt to submit unsorted cell_indices (e.g., [2, 1, 0, 3]) and verify rejection. 5. Test edge cases: adjacent duplicates, non-adjacent duplicates, descending order, equal adjacent values. 6. Submit duplicate cell_indices with CONFLICTING cell data and verify: (a) rejection occurs before interpolation, (b) no partial processing or state changes. 7. Verify the error response does not leak internal state. 8. Check that validation happens before any cryptographic operations.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-15, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Duplicate/unsorted cell_indices with conflicting data causes incorrect polynomial interpolation.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does polynomial interpolation assume unique, sorted cell_indices?

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review the polynomial interpolation algorithm used in recovery. 2. Identify any assumptions about input uniqueness or ordering in the interpolation code. 3. Determine if duplicate x-coordinates (cell_indices) would cause: division by zero, undefined behavior, or silent incorrect results. 4. Trace the data flow from cell_indices validation to interpolation call. 5. Verify no path exists where unvalidated cell_indices reach the interpolation function. 6. Check for defensive programming: does the interpolation function have its own validation? 7. Assess if memory safety issues could arise from duplicate indices (buffer overflows, out-of-bounds access).
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-15, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Polynomial interpolation requires unique x-coordinates; duplicates may cause undefined behavior.
